rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty builder trees go (a row of ficus, eucalyptus, magnolias and jacarandas along the back fences, two palms, a norfolk pine and a magnolia 3 m from the house fronts); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the adirondack chair, the grills, two swing sets and the open south lot corners.

trees.why: the back yard with the adirondack chair (1.7 m off): a jacaranda to sit under
the back yard with the two kettle grills: shade over the cooks
the yard with the swing set (2.6 m off): a young eucalyptus over the swings
the south yard with the swing set (2.8 m off): shade over the swings
the open lot corner at the south-west, 24 m from the walls: a full magnolia
the south back lot line between two yards, 9 m from the houses: shade for both
